body:
I got the same error but I have managed to make an MRP of it

This bug is possibly related to: #95027 and #56066

System info is:

> Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19043) - Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon(TM)  Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21921.1000) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600G with Radeon Graphics (12 threads)

Godot build is:

> v4.5.dev.custom_build [5e27318b6] (same mrp as 4.4.1-stable, built from source)
> v4.5.dev4.official [209a446e3] (same mrp as 4.4.1-stable)
> v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6] [fsr2-bug-mrp3.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20218599/fsr2-bug-mrp3.zip)
>  v4.2.stable.official [46dc27791] [fsr2-bug-mrp4-godot4-2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20224274/fsr2-bug-mrp4-godot4-2.zip)

Behavior is exactly the same between all versions tested (the MRP will reproduce it) but most testing has been done with v4.4.1-stable.

The line mentioned in the error is:

> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/effects/fsr2.cpp#L418 - my uneducated guess is the error has to do with what mip levels are generated on a viewport that's too small or something and this line isn't the actual problem but I'm adding it here for convenience.

Attached is the MRP project. It has no `.godot` folder or anything other than what is needed. FSR2 should be active in the project settings. The MRP works by having 2 cameras, one looking at a MeshInstance3D with the default godot svg icon as its texture, default import settings, the other one looking at a MeshInstance3D with a ViewportTexture as its Albedo, showing the first camera's view. The error occurs when the SubViewport is set to dimensions too low, with FSR2 active, and the project is run at least once.

Steps to reproduce with MRP:

  1. Ensure FSR2 is active in the project settings and the SubViewport (just the SubViewport is likely enough though)
  2. Set SubViewport scaling to 1.0 or less, preferrably less (or leave it at 0.67 in the MRP)
  3. Set SubViewport render dimensions to 64x64 (from inspector, just to be clear I don't mean node dimensions) 
  4. If error spam doesn't start, run the project. Error spam should start and it should continue inside the editor now.
To stop the error, set at least one of X or Y in the dimensions of the SubViewport to 96 pixels or larger (for the MRP that has a render scale of 0.67 - this number depends on the render scale used). The error spam should stop.

From now on (presumably unless the `.godot` folder is deleted) when the project is loaded **and both** of the dimensions of the SubViewport are below `64 / render_scale` in pixels (which for the MRP is 96px since the render scale is set to 0.67 - for a render scale of 0.25 at least one of the dimensions has to be 256px or above), you will get the error spam on project load, as long as the SubViewport is in the 3d view. Also, the error spam does not stop if the SubViewport is hidden or its parent is hidden: either the conditions have to be fixed (the ones mentioned above) or it has to be deleted from the scene for the error to stop.

The import settings on the image (specifically generating mipmaps) seem to have no effect, neither does the Sampling option in the material of the MeshInstance3D which is used to display the ViewportTexture (so setting it to something like Linear instead of Linear Mipmap does not fix the error). Changing the Texture Mipmap option from the default 0.0 has no effect. The error still occurs at a render scale of 1.0, at which point at least one dimension must be 64px (at render scales above 1.0 the editor falls back to Bilinear).

---

_Addendum: I'm not sure if this is related or a separate issue but attempting to set the SubViewport dimensions below 3px can cause the editor to crash, if FSR2 is active on the SubViewport itself. If the scaling is anything other than FSR2 or the render scale is 1.0, the editor allows setting either of the viewport dimensions as low as 2px and no lower and does not crash._

_There was a glitch related to non-even dimensions (such as 255x64) while the error conditions were true but I can't reproduce._

I think you are onto something. In my game, I enable FSR 2 and set `Viewport::scaling_3d_scale` to 0.25 in my settings.
Then, once I reload my scene or if I restart the game, I get a crash when loading back into the scene.

Interestingly, it doesn't crash immediately when I apply the settings (I can see FSR 2 working with 0.25 scale), but only once I've (re)loaded my scene (which contains my camera).

Do you have any subviewports in your scene (especially ones that are small or can change size) or change resolution dynamically on either the main viewport or subviewports? Also do you see any errors in the output? When you say it doesn't crash immediately, does it still crash instantly when you reload your scene? Perhaps that's similar to what happens when the MRP is loaded (where it needs to be run before every condition is in place for the error spam). If you don't have subviewports in your scene, it might be a way to figure out what else can reproduce the crash.

I've found a reliable way to reproduce the crash.
```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var vp := SubViewport.new()
	add_child(vp);
	
	vp.scaling_3d_scale = 0.25
	vp.scaling_3d_mode = Viewport.SCALING_3D_MODE_FSR2
	vp.set_size(Vector2i(2, 2));
	vp.set_update_mode(SubViewport.UPDATE_ONCE);

	var cam := Camera3D.new()
	vp.add_child(cam);
```

These are the errors I get as well, it looks like it is occurring because it is trying to allocate a texture the size of 2 *0.25.
```yaml
ERROR: Condition "p_job.uavMip[i] >= mip_slice_rids.size()" is true. Returning: FFX_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
   at: execute_gpu_job_compute_rd (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/effects/fsr2.cpp:418)
ERROR: Width must be equal or greater than 1 for all textures
   at: texture_create (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:898)
ERROR: Condition "texture.is_null()" is true. Returning: FFX_ERROR_BACKEND_API_ERROR
   at: create_resource_rd (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/effects/fsr2.cpp:241)
```

By default in `Viewport` constructor it applies scaling 3d configs from `ProjectSettings` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/45fc515ae3574e9c1f9deacaa6960dec68a7d38b/scene/main/viewport.cpp#L5338-L5339
So if you were to have a viewport with a small size, and your project settings has FSR2 and 3d scale set to 0.25, you will get a hard crash.

This is affecting Terrain3D due to this https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/blob/37fb986cad4f6b1e87036450ee55f9bd3917ef3a/src/terrain_3d.cpp#L217
So to mitigate it until the bug gets fixed in godot, maybe @TokisanGames can add this as a workaround?
```cpp
_mouse_vp->set_scaling_3d_mode(Viewport::SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR)
```

Good catch on the Terrain3D code, that looks like the guilty line when it comes to the FSR2 crash. The workaround should work, though I can't test it at the moment.

I think the errors you're getting are separate from the FSR2 crash. The editor will not allow going below a 2x2 size on a viewport, my guess is it probably doesn't allow any texture below 2x2 anywhere, so even if this was fixed, those errors would likely show up anyway (unless you've tested this without FSR2 and the errors don't occur | edit - I did see that in the code the hard limit is for textures not being below 0 on either dimension so perhaps this is also related to FSR2). This does give us a handy workaround through code though, so 👍

The filtering can be changed from the inspector if this is going to be a static subviewport in the scene (as in, not generated by code) but the editor currently will switch subviewport properties to the ones in the project settings on new subviewports at least, though it seems it changed the settings on the subviewport I already had in the scene as well. I'm not sure if the behavior is consistent there but I haven't tested this to see if there is some unpredictable behavior happening.

edit - also, this seems to only occur for small subviewports so I'm not sure if there is much benefit to keeping FSR2 active if the texture size is too small. Given the relationship between minimum size and scaling factor I mentioned above, it might be acceptable to implement bilinear as a fallback to FSR2 if the viewport drops below the critical size.

In related issues, for example for mipmap generation breaking at low sizes, disabling mipmaps has been suggested as a workaround: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56066#issuecomment-1522333109. And it seems glow can break under the same conditions: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56066#issuecomment-997313966. There is already a fallback to Bilinear when FSR2 scaling is set above 1.0, so I feel like this is a reasonable fix.

>	_mouse_vp->set_scaling_3d_mode(Viewport::SCALING_3D_MODE_BILINEAR);

Great, thanks for the fix. Committed in https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/commit/df5afe4541beaf322173c5f2bcfa2b61b7fae57e.

This resolves the reported error for me, and I would close the issue. But it seems like the outstanding Godot issue is two fold. Let's see if I have the summary correct. I was able to produce these two in a new project, adding a subviewport, a camera, and setting these on the sbv:
* Error spam
  * Viewport < 256x256, FSR2, 3D Scaling <= 0.3
  * Viewport < 64x64, FSR2, 3D Scaling 1
* Crash 
  * Viewport 2x2, FSR2, 3D Scaling < 1
  * Viewport <8x8, FSR2, 3D Scaling < .3


Is this everything?

Yes that is the reproduction we have so far on this.

I don't think the issue should be closed since this wasn't specific to your project and it should stay open so it can be tracked until some fix exists in core so it doesn't happen. It also serves as a place for people to find details and a workaround for now.

I looked into the code yesterday (Godot's) starting from this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/servers/rendering/renderer_viewport.cpp#L184 and I plan to look into it further, combining the issues I linked (since at least mipmap generation is related) so that I can submit a temporary fix so that it falls back to Bilinear in all these cases, once I have time. That way we can at least avoid the error spam. I feel like a proper fix would require adjusting the FSR2 code (since the crash can happen when the viewport is set through code) but I don't understand enough about the rendering or FSR2 to have any confidence in making changes there.

Either way, at least now we have a clear reproduction and a workaround 👍. If nothing else, this allows some warning to be placed in the editor and documentation.
